text: [L18-L19] (MED/build-order-coupling) The executable post-build deletes the entire shared distribution directory, including library DLLs published by the library post-build scripts.
[L22,L25-L26] (MED/stale-packaging) TargetDir is never cleared before wildcard packaging, allowing stale executables and DLLs from earlier builds to enter the new distribution.
[L1074-L1081] (MED/platform-version-matching) The Darwin undefined-symbol policy has no matching branch for explicit deployment targets beginning with 11 or later.
[L5157,L5862,L6731] (MED/variable-name) The OS/2 branches assign old_archive_From_new_cmds with an uppercase F instead of the declared old_archive_from_new_cmds variable.

[L5149-L5154,L5854-L5859,L6723-L6728] (MED/shell-command-construction) The OS/2 prefix_cmds string embeds shell quotes but is expanded as a command without eval, leaving those quotes literal in the sed arguments.

[L6043-L6047,L7144-L7146,L7155-L7158,L7187-L7189] (LOW/platform-matching) Several branches match the full host triplet against bare sysv4 or osf3 patterns, preventing their intended platform-specific handling.
[L7537-L7538] (MED/dependency-parser) The separated -L and -R flag test prefixes only its left operands with x, so those flags cannot match and their following directory arguments are lost.
[L96-L108] (MED/configuration-contamination) IFX executable builds reuse classic intermediate directories, permitting stale objects when switching compiler projects.

[L23-L29] (MED/destructive-staging) Both distributed DLLs are deleted before source existence or copy success is established, so missing inputs can erase previously usable artifacts without failing explicitly.

[L6,L17-L18,L23-L29] (MED/build-order-coupling) Each library's post-build invocation republishes both libraries from fixed directories while ignoring TargetDir, allowing stale counterpart binaries or concurrent post-build interference.
[L13] (LOW/locale-dependence) Build_Date slices DATE at fixed character offsets, producing malformed dates under different Windows locale formats.
[L6-L15] (MED/batch-expansion) RevisionNumber is interpolated directly into an echoed Fortran literal without escaping, so quotes or command metacharacters can corrupt generation.
[L20] (MED/stale-packaging) Adding into an existing ZIP does not remove entries whose source files disappeared, so repeated packaging can retain obsolete artifacts.

[L16,L20,L26] (LOW/packaging-side-effects) The script temporarily overwrites a destination 7za.exe and then deletes it unconditionally, with no distinction between its temporary copy and a pre-existing file.
[L84-L87] (MED/stale-provenance) version.dat has no prerequisites or forced refresh, so incremental rebuilds retain obsolete revision and build-date metadata.
[L111-L112] (MED/clean-rule) CLEANFILES includes every local *.inc file and therefore removes the distributed nh_pars.inc during an in-source clean.
[L96-L97,L107-L108] (MED/configuration-contamination) IFX builds share intermediate and module directories with the classic BMI project, allowing stale products across compiler switches.

[L256-L260,L334-L335,L343-L350] (MED/incremental-dependencies) Included Fortran files are prerequisites of the archive rather than its compiled objects, so changing an include can relink stale object code.

[L76-L78,L343-L350,L496,L602-L605] (MED/parallel-build) Module targets trigger ordinary .o compilation while the library independently triggers .lo compilation of the same sources, allowing concurrent writes to the same module files.
[L31,L50,L164,L183] (MED/cache-key) The repeatable line-length macros share one cache entry per language across different requested lengths and source formats.
[L104-L115] (MED/feature-probe) The preprocessing test contains no code that requires preprocessing, allowing compilers that ignore directives and unknown options to produce a false positive.

[L96-L97,L107-L108] (MED/configuration-contamination) IFX builds reuse the classic project's intermediate and module directories, allowing stale compiler-specific build products to be reused when switching projects.
[L96-L108] (MED/configuration-contamination) IFX static builds use the same intermediate and module directories as classic builds, leaving compiler-switch stale-product contamination possible.

[L21-L24,L37-L38,L49] (MED/incremental-dependencies) Included Fortran sources are declared as library dependencies instead of object dependencies, so edits can relink the library without recompiling the affected code.

[L18,L34,L40,L48,L51,L65-L74] (MED/parallel-build) The convenience library generates .lo objects while module targets request separate .o objects from the same sources, allowing competing module-file generation.
